text.p: Financial analysts said they were pleased with the first half results of Rhone-Poulenc SA because they came in at the high end of expectations and its 20 percent 1997 EPS growth target seemed within reach.
"It was a pleasant surprise," said Hans Zuyd of Paribas in London. "We were expecting 1.55 billion, so it was slightly higher, he said.
"It is always nice to see that a higher range has been met, especially when you see the improvement in the chemicals and the fibres sectors, they seem to be doing quite well there," Zuyd said.
He noted restructuring costs were down.
He plans to maintain his 1997 net income forecast at 3.4 billion francs.
Rhone reported a 14 percent rise in first half earnings to 1.608 billion francs.
Financial analysts said they were awaiting the outcome of teleconference briefings, at 0800 GMT in French and 1230 GMT in English, before drawing full conclusions.
At Merill Lynch an analyst said the house would not raise its forecast but he was pleased with the results.
"The figures show that the company is progressing well, against the background of its restructuring and the current environment," he said.
"They seem to feel that they can reach their 20 percent (1997 EPS growth) target but I do not think that we are upgrading our forecast," he added.
Brokerage Ferri said it was increasing its 1997 profit forecast to 3.425 billion from 3,325 billion and remained positive on the share.

"The results are very encouraging as far as the outlook improvement in fibres and chemicals is concerned, even if there may have been some stock replenishing in polyamide which could depress sales in the second half," the broker said in a note.
At 0858 GMT, Rhone shares were up 2.62 percent at 255 francs. "Maybe some people were very surprised," Paribas' Zuyd said, adding Rhone had recently underperformed other chemical shares.
